results.text: not valuable . entrance fees costly get nothing. just hang round 10 minute. It can be good temple for hindus people

results.title: Thought provoking
results.text: Remarkable site - we didn't use a guide but wandered, sat and contemplated the different culture we saw.

results.title: worth a visit
results.text: Whilst non-Hindu's don't have access to the main temple, you have the opportunity to see cremations happening along the river, which is an interesting experience. There is also a homeless shelter for elderly Nepalis which you can visit.

results.title: Gods own place
results.text: The temple management is very good. Temple Management offers POOJA on request. So if you want to go for Rudrabhishek, or Mahamritunjay Jaap etc just contact Temple. No need to book from Out side Pujari ( Priest).

results.title: Very Conscientious Priest
results.text: Very sacred Hindu temple complex. Our priest made sure we did all the rituals while he conducted a 20 minute puja to ensure that we were blessed with the Grace of the Almighty.

results.title: A life and death experience, not for the fainthearted
results.text: This is the second most important Hindu burial site after Benares/Varanasi in India. The main temple is not to be entered by non-Hindus, but even so one can walk around in a Necropolis of white temple structures. This is an active and very busy cremation site, so pick a day when you're in the mood to face the liminal experience of being accosted by hopeful tourist guides right next to groups of relatives bewailing the passing of a loved one as scavengers search the river for gold teeth or jewelry left behind from earlier cremations.

results.title: Sacred Offerings, Sacred Returns
results.text: A place for spiritual and religious seekers. A place for prayers and a place for learning by observing how believers dedicate themselves and surrender to the powers of the temple complex. Keep in mind that going inside the praying complex is only for Buddhist and Hindus, but nobody asked me what I was. So, if your go with respect and sincere desire to pray and not to hang out the photographing tourist, you may enter smoothly. Enjoy!

results.title: Just soak it all up.
results.text:
This is a very important site for Hindus and has an amazing atmosphere of a religion in action. As a foreign tourist, you are superfluous, except for the inevitable scams and fakes that you should obviously avoid. Most of the visitors are not camera wielding Europeans or Americans but religious tourists from Nepal and other parts of the sub-continent. Some visitors have problems with Pashupatinath:
               1. "Those burning bodies were gross!"
               2. "It's so so rude to say that only Hindus are allowed in the Temple"
Ref. 1. This site is revered and famous for its cemetery ghats. If you are that squeamish it would be better not to go. But a great pity as this is an important aspect of life, (and death), in Nepal.
Ref.2.  I felt much happier knowing where I could and could not go. It seems perfectly reasonable to reserve some areas for practising Hindus where they can make their religious observances away from our prying and camera snapping eyes. Few of us would object to the common signs in English Cathedrals "this chapel is reserved for silent prayer". It's not really that different.
This was my 3rd visit to Pashupatinath in the last few years and I nearly didn't go as I had been to Varanasi, (world's most famous cemetery ghats?) earlier on the trip and felt that Pashupatinath would be a pale shadow of that site. However, I was wrong and now feel that this site is a unique and special place and like Bodunath Stupa is a useful reminder that Nepal is a country steeped in a complex mix of fervently held religious beliefs, irrespective of our own views.
Unlike several other reviewers, I would advise anyone to avoid a guide, however authoritative and cheap they are. It is so easy to end up like a school child on a trip, where the endless transmission of facts, figures and information actually stops you from just experiencing the place in your own way. So my advice is........"Just soak it all up!"

results.title: Do visit and have some respect...
results.text:
You can't go inside the temple if you are not Hindu. But still it's worth to see the cremation site. It's best to go in the morning as not so many people visit the place. It gets crowded in the afternoon. Be careful with the guides, they are not professional guides.

Have also one thing in mind - this is a cremation site . It's someone's funeral . I see this tourist with big cameras taking photos at someones funeral with no respect. I felt terrible for the families who burned their loved ones.
Think how would you feel if someone for touristic reasons would take photos at the funeral of your loved one ?
Have a heart and some respect.

results.title: old temple
results.text: temple is old and maintained well. there are many monkeys in temple especially near the main deity area though they do not disturb the worshippers. the main deity doors open only during aarti, which is in morning and in the evening.

results.title: Nice but not at itsbest
results.text: Most of the places for Budh religion are very clean and tidy but i saw some of those in Nepal which were not but nonetheless this was clean and just not properly managed but still a must see and also If you are interested in gettiing clicked in traditional Nepali dress it is possible at this location.

results.title: Always something interesting going on
results.text: I visited 1 day after Maha shivarati and the temple grounds were still full of sadhus from all over Nepal and India...the cremation process and locals seeking sadhus to perform some simple chants and rituals are interesting to watch. I walked from Boudanath to Pashupatinath so visitors can easily put this 2 attractions in the same day's itinerary.

results.title: Fantastic!
results.text: A big, picturesque temple complex. The fee is a bit expensive for foreigners (not so much for SAARC countries) but it's really worth it. Peaceful atmosphere amongst monkeys and sadhus. Nice views of Kathmandu from the top. Fantastic experience!

results.title: pashupatinath
results.text: This place is most holi place in kathmandu but please don't take pictures of burning place for the rest you can take pictures as forever you are not allow to entering the temple the price is 1000 NPR place respect this place

results.title: Surreal
results.text: We were there a day before Maha Shivratri ( Lord Shiva's Birthday) and it was simply outstanding... unfortunately one is not allowed to click pictures inside the temple .... but trust me.. if you love photography ..it is just a must visit place...there is chaos and serenity at the same time

results.title: A very moving experience
results.text: This is a sacred Hindu site and has cremations occurring whilst tourists are passing by, the whole complex has lots of interesting parts for the visitor. Apart from the rather inappropriate behaviour of some tourists, I found the experience here emotional and a fascinating insight into other belief systems. Some have commented about fake guides etc but I would not travel around this area without a knowledgeable and experienced guide.

results.title: Get a guide
results.text:
We navigated the place on our own, which you can certainly do. However, I recommend paying for a guide just so that you don't get hassled the entire time you are there. There were a couple of cremations going on and there were monkeys running around everywhere. 
Lots of poverty and people with deformities begging for money.any people dressed up ( be prepared to tip them if you take any photos)

results.title: A Fascinating Place
results.text:
I loved the whole Pashupatinah complex - the temples, the colors, the solemn cremation sites,the sadhus, and the market place.
We had an excellent guide. His name is Sumit Kharel 9813987133. Email: sumit.kharel@yahoo.com. Thanks Sumit! You shared so much in a delightful way.
This was a very memorable experience and you made it doubly so.

results.title: an oppressive feeling
results.text:
I visited the Pashupatinath temple and felt really oppressed from the entrance until the exit! The entrance price is way too expensive comparing to other temples but also comparing to the overall visit. You cannot enter the main temple and you are constantly harassed by beggars, tourist guides, or gurus. Be careful of those people as they will come to you, paint your forehead with a colour point without asking, and then ask for money (plus these painting may give allergies to some people so be careful).
Finally the body cremation is not really attractive and the smell is awful.
I saw some monkey but very few compared to the buddhist monkey temple where there are loads of them.

results.title: Authentic but be careful
results.text:
Went only to the cremation part, not to the zoo or park. 
It's very authentic. There were actually some cremation ceremonies taking place. 
However be careful for the fake guides and all the scam going on there. Right after you enter the site some noon official guide will offer you guided visit. Price will be outrageous of course. The tour is 30 mins. You can choose to take the tour, it can come out as great and you'll learn and feel more about the place than by going alone. However if you do so don't pay over 500 NPR in TOTAL (at first they will ask for 1000NPR per person which is just insane)
They will also try to bring you to other places like the Buddhist temple or the zoo in exchange for some more money... Up to you but this is extra charge of course.
